value.text:
The user wants me to act as Evidence Critic and check each claim against the cited evidence. I need to flag only factual problems: overstatements, wrong numbers/dates/suppliers, causes not stated, products/NDCs not in evidence. Reasonable conclusions from cited facts are supported.

Let me examine each claim:

Claim 1: investigator: "Our package NDC 0703-3671-01 is on the FDA shortage list with limited availability, FDA reason category Other, estimated recovery October 2026." Cited: [shortage-0703-3671-01]

Evidence says: "FDA shortage list: Methotrexate Sodium Preservative Free, Injection, 25 mg/1 mL (NDC 0703-3671-01) from Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc.; availability: "Limited Availability"; FDA reason category: "Other"; estimated recovery: October 2026; updated 10/15/2026"

This matches exactly. The claim says "limited availability" (lowercase) but evidence says "Limited Availability". That's the same. Supported.

Claim 2: investigator: "Current stock of 50 units covers 51.7 days at 1 unit per day, with an open order of 38 units expected 2026-10-16." Cited: [stock-6]

Evidence says: "methotrexate METHOTREXATE SODIUM 25 mg/mL (Teva Parenteral Medicines, Inc., NDC 0703-3671-01, ANDA040843): 50 units on hand, 1/day over 30 days, 51.7 days of cover; open orders: PO-SAMPLE-006 open 38 units from AmerisourceBergen, expected 2026-10-16"

Matches exactly. Supported.

Claim 3: investigator: "No ongoing recall for this NDC." Cited: [search-recall-6]

Evidence says: "Searched this run's FDA ongoing-recall snapshot for our package NDC 0703-3671-01 and product 0703-3671: no ongoing recall."

Matches. Supported.

All claims appear supported. No factual problems. So unsupported list empty.
